messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: synth-canary-eu1 FAILED (firing) -> 74 probes failed in 2m across eu1 / probe-group-lookup. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Alert details: service=synthetic-canaries, severity=critical, dedupe_count=3. Auto-suppression policy: threshold=60/sec. No ack yet.

Jay: acked via PagerDuty. I'm oncall for the next 30m. Kicking off triage. @Erin can you grab canary-runner logs and check error types?

Erin: looking now. Seeing massive 401 responses on the probe target in eu1. Querying canary-runner aggregated metrics.

canary-runner: log snippet (aggregated):
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z probe_id=eu1-lookup status=401 upstream=auth-service-eu path=/v1/token latency=32ms
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z probe_id=eu1-lookup status=401 upstream=auth-service-eu path=/v1/token latency=28ms
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z probe_id=eu1-lookup status=200 upstream=backend-eu path=/health latency=15ms
2026-03-15T14:02:14Z probe_id=eu1-lookup status=401 upstream=auth-service-eu path=/v1/token latency=30ms
```

Erin: the failing step is token acquisition from auth-service-eu. Probes failing when they try to get a token. Not a canary runtime crash.

Lee: @Erin can you confirm whether auth-service-eu had a deploy or certificate rotation in the last hour? Checking infra dashboards.

Erin: no deploys recorded in prometheus.deployment.events for auth-service-eu in the last 90m. TLS cert expiry check: cert not expired. Error body shows "invalid_client" from upstream. That smells like a client credential issue.

Priya: Support reported a small spike in error reports for EU customers on embedding endpoints ~14:01-14:03. Roughly 0.3% of requests failed with 401. Not widespread but noticeable for dashboards.

Ana: Product - is customer-facing functionality impacted? Any major customers?

Priya: mostly internal monitoring and a few low-volume API keys; no high-paying customers flagged yet. I'm contacting a couple of accounts and will escalate if needed.

Jay: ok, initial impact: synthetic probes and a small fraction of API requests in eu region due to token exchange 401 from auth-service-eu. Triage plan: (1) reduce probe fanout to stop pager flood, (2) confirm auth-service client creds, (3) add temporary probe fallback to alternate auth endpoint, (4) if persistence, rollback recent changes to auth gateway config.

Erin: reducing probe fanout now by toggling probe-group-lookup config -> target_rate from 100rps to 10rps. Command: 
```
# runbook: throttle canary probes
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/probes/lookup/config -d '{"target_rate":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

canary-runner: probe rate change applied; observing fanout drop. New failures ~6 in 2m. Pager noise should reduce.

pagerduty-bot: Auto-suppression: 52 similar pages suppressed while probe rate changed. Current alert still active (critical).

Lee: investigating auth-service-eu client credential store (vault path: secret/services/auth-service/clients). Pulling audit log.

Erin: also launching targeted curl against auth-service-eu token endpoint with known working client id (rotated) to reproduce.

Erin: curl output:
```
$ curl -kv -X POST https://auth-eu.internal/v1/token -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=canary-client'
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_client", "error_description": "Client credentials are invalid" }
```

Lee: audit logs show a config change 14:00 UTC to the client registry from CI: automated-key-rotation-job. It rotated a subset of client secrets and didn't update the mapping for canary-client. That aligns.

Jay: who owns the key rotation job? @Erin any reason rotation would skip canary-client?

Erin: rotation job is owned by infra team; there was an exclude list but it looks like the canary-client got included by mistake.

Lee: I can re-insert the old secret for canary-client into the vault and trigger auth-service to reload. Doing that now (vault write + service reload).

Lee: performed vault write and POST /reload to auth-service-eu. Waiting for cache TTL.

canary-runner: after reload, token exchange success rate improving: 200/210 requests success in last 30s. Failures falling to baseline.

Priya: support - customer error rate back to normal for EU. Noticing a few delayed webhook retries but nothing customer-impacting now.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: alert resolved (auto) - no manual close necessary.

Jay: marking incident as mitigated. Root cause: automated key rotation job incorrectly rotated canary-client secret without updating mapping -> auth-service returned invalid_client to probes and a small subset of API calls.

Erin: immediate mitigation: reinserted previous secret and forced auth-service-eu reload. Long term: add canary-client to rotation exclude list and tighten rotation job verification. Also add canary test in rotation pipeline to validate token exchange post-rotation.

Lee: follow-ups (postmortem actions):
- infra: patch rotation job to respect exclude list (owner: Lee)
- infra: add canary client validation step to rotation pipeline (owner: Lee)
- sre: add runbook step to throttle probes automatically on auth failures to prevent alert storms (owner: Erin)
- product/support: send customer note if any affected customers report issues (owner: Ana/Priya)

Ana: I can draft a short internal note and a potential external blurb if needed.

Jay: good work. Closing actions assigned. Will schedule post-incident review tomorrow 1100 UTC.

Erin: adding brief incident timeline to #postmortems after review.

Priya: will follow up if any customers reply.

incident-bot: Thread closed by Jay. Summary and runbook links: https://docs.internal/runbooks/canary-auth-rotation ; postmortem ticket: PM-4521
